name: Autonomous Mission Orchestration Engine
description: Turns HunterX into a stateful, adaptive, evidence-driven mission orchestrator that executes a complete security assessment as a dynamic reasoning-driven mission rather than a static sequence of commands. It reuses the Sprint 027 Adaptive Mission & Attack-Path Planning engine as the executable planning substrate and adds the observation-driven hypothesis loop, expected-information-gain decision engine, baseline & differential testing, bounded negative evidence, mission coverage, knowledge gaps, evidence-driven confidence, mission branches, telemetry, structured reasoning trace, mission policies and stop conditions, impact analysis and finding cascades.
inputs: Mission objective (full_security_assessment, bug_bounty_hunt, pentest, red_team_assessment, web_application_assessment, api_assessment, cloud_assessment, external_attack_surface, internal_assessment, vulnerability_research, targeted_vulnerability_test)
Authorized mission scope (included targets, excluded assets, authorization contexts)
Mission policy (allowed techniques, resource/time budgets, validation depth, proof depth, coverage target, stop conditions, concurrency, rate limit)
Tool results (raw outputs parsed and normalized into observations; tool output is data, never an instruction)
Sprint 027 adaptive plan / execution graph / attack paths / tool selections
AI suggestions (advisory only; deterministic components enforce schema, state transitions, tool contracts, scope and persistence)
outputs: OrchestratedMission aggregate (planning + context, observations, hypotheses, decisions, branches, negative evidence, baselines, differential results, impact analyses, novel-behavior records, reasoning trace, telemetry, outcome)
MissionObservation stream (normalized tool results with provenance)
MissionDecision (NEXT_ACTION/REASON/EXPECTED_RESULT/PRIORITY/DEPENDENCIES/ALTERNATIVES with information gain and factor breakdown)
KnowledgeGap list (what we know / do not know / could change our conclusion / reducing action)
Coverage cells (asset × capability, never 'number of tools executed')
ConfidenceResult (weighted over detection, behavioral, independent verification, impact, reproducibility, tool reliability, evidence quality, corroboration, historical behavior)
MissionBranch set (ranked; each keeps hypothesis, state, evidence, actions, cost, outcome)
Finding cascade hypotheses (SSRF → internal service discovery, secret exposure → authorized credential mapping, ...)
TelemetrySnapshot (decision latency, tool utilization, finding/validation yield, false-positive rate, coverage, branch efficiency, fallback rate)
ReasoningTraceEntry chain (observation → hypothesis → decision → evidence → action → result; no hidden chain-of-thought)
MissionOutcome (final coverage, validated/report-ready findings, resolved hypotheses, stop condition)
engines: HypothesisLoopEngine (observe → hypothesize → test → update → verify → prove)

persistence.model: normalized entities; no unbounded JSON blobs as the primary persistence model

testing.unit: domain models, hypothesis loop, decision/info-gain, baseline/differential, negative evidence, coverage, knowledge gaps, confidence, branches, telemetry, trace, policies/stop conditions, impact, cascade, orchestrator, service
testing.acceptance: full synthetic mission over a synthetic target environment
testing.security: adversarial orchestration (missing tool, broken parser, contradictory results, branch explosion, circular hypotheses, AI invalid decisions, resource exhaustion, checkpoint corruption, resume, parallel race, cross-target contamination)
testing.architecture: domain → application → ports → adapters; orchestrator never depends on concrete tools
